answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity registry: before an agent transacts, it must lock a stake behind a hardware-attested key, and peers can challenge suspicious identities. A sybil farm therefore has to post real, slashable capital for every account it creates; any identity proven to be a duplicate is slashed and evicted. Like a quartz oscillator holding one stable frequency, the registry keeps identities expensive to clone, so a manufactured crowd cannot ripple through the market unnoticed. Each additional voice must carry its own funded signal, making faking one unprofitable.
